# Castle sequence catalogue

## What this is

This page catalogues the sequences that castles produce, organized by the castle object each one counts rather than by OEIS A-number. Each row gives first terms, a recurrence or generating function (g.f.), its growth constant, and the entry of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS) it equals, at the stated offset; "-" means no entry is listed.[^1]

This page and [[oeis-index](pages/oeis-index.md)] are generated by `bin/generate-sequence-pages.py` from one data file, `config/castle-sequences.tsv`: this page shows its rows by family, and the index shows its A-numbers with the pages that cite them. [[oeis-cross-referencing](pages/oeis-cross-referencing.md)] describes the checks a match must pass, [[oeis-mining-pe502](pages/oeis-mining-pe502.md)] collects the castle counts matched to OEIS entries, and [[oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles](pages/oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles.md)] proves the height-2 rows.

The symbols are those of [[castle-notation](pages/castle-notation.md)]: `A^e(w, h)` and `A^o(w, h)` count the castles of width `w` and height `h` with an even and an odd number of blocks. A skyline on `{1, …, h}` need not reach height `h`, so a count of skylines on `{1, …, h}` is a count of castles of every height up to `h`.

## Catalogue

### Multi-interpretation hub

`A005251` (`0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 12, 21, 37, …` from `n = 0`, growth `ψ² = 1.7549`, with `ψ` the plastic number) counts six objects: the tree castles of area `n`, four more in explicit bijection with them, and the even-sector signed towers, equal in number by a change of basis ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]):

| object | first terms | g.f. / formula | OEIS |
|---|---|---|---|
| tree castles of area `n`, any height (compositions of `n` with no two adjacent parts `≥ 2`) | `1, 2, 4, 7, 12, …` from `n = 1` | - | [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251) (`= A005251(n+2)`) |
| binary strings of length `N` with no factor `010` | `1, 2, 4, 7, 12, …` from `N = 0` | the gap map, `N = n − 1` | [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251) (`= A005251(N+3)`) |
| Hardin's binary words of length `N` with no isolated 1, `W_1(N)` | `1, 2, 4, 7, 12, …` from `N = 1` | the column map, `N = n` | [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251) (`= A005251(N+2)`) |
| compositions of `m` with no part 2 | `1, 1, 2, 4, 7, …` from `m = 1` | the leading-column map, `m = n + 1` | [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251) (`= A005251(m+1)`) |
| tower-spacing skylines `(h = 2, g = 2)` of width `w` | `2, 4, 7, 12, 21, …` from `w = 1` | the gap map, then the complement, `w = n − 1` | [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251) (`= A005251(w+3)`) |
| `P_even(6, L)/2^L`, the even-sector signed towers | `1, 2, 4, 7, …` from `L = 0` | equal counts by a change of basis, `L = n − 1` | [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251) (`= A005251(L+3)`) |

The gap map takes a composition of `n` to a binary string of length `n − 1`, a part `c` becoming `c − 1` zeros and the parts joined by single `1`s, and "no two adjacent parts `≥ 2`" to "no factor `010`". The complement of that string is the second row of a tower-spacing skyline of width `n − 1` with `g = 2`, which has no factor `101`. The column map sends a column of height 1 to `0` and a column of height `c ≥ 2` to `1^c`. See [[plastic-number](pages/plastic-number.md)].

### Tree castles of area n by block parity

A tree castle of area `n` and width `w` has `1 + n − w` blocks, one more than the number of zeros of its string, and by the parity of the number of blocks the tree castles of area `n` split as follows ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]). Terms from `n = 1`.

| object | first terms | g.f. / formula | OEIS |
|---|---|---|---|
| tree castles of area `n`, even number of blocks | `0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 11, 18, 33, 56, 101, 174, 310, 538, 952` | `(A005251(n+2) + (−1)^n A000931(n−1))/2` | - |
| tree castles of area `n`, odd number of blocks | `1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 10, 19, 32, 58, 99, 177, 306, 543, 945` | `(A005251(n+2) − (−1)^n A000931(n−1))/2` | - |
| even minus odd | `−1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, −1, 1, −2, 2, −3, 4, −5, 7` | `−q(1 − q²)/(1 − q² + q³)` | [A000931](https://oeis.org/A000931) (`= (−1)^n A000931(n−1)`) Padovan, signed |

*(Every row agrees with enumeration for `n ≤ 20`; the OEIS has no match for the even row from `n = 2` to 13 or the odd row from `n = 1` to 13, 2026-10-25.)*

### Castles by area with bounded height: the n-nacci family

A castle of area `n` is a composition of `n`, its column heights in order ([[castles-of-height-h-by-area](pages/castles-of-height-h-by-area.md)]). The castles of height at most `h` are the compositions with parts at most `h`, counted by the `h`-step Fibonacci numbers with g.f. `1/(1 − x − ⋯ − x^h)`; the castles of height 2 are the compositions into parts 1 and 2 that use a 2, `F_{n+1} − 1` of them.

| object | from | first terms | growth | OEIS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| height 2 | `n = 1…` | `0, 1, 2, 4, 7, 12, 20, 33` | `φ` | [A000071](https://oeis.org/A000071) (`= A000071(n+1) = F_{n+1} − 1`) |
| height at most 3 | `n = 1…` | `1, 2, 4, 7, 13, 24, 44, 81` | tribonacci `1.8393` | [A000073](https://oeis.org/A000073) (`= A000073(n+2)`) |
| height at most 4 | `n = 1…` | `1, 2, 4, 8, 15, 29, 56, 108` | tetranacci `1.9276` | [A000078](https://oeis.org/A000078) (`= A000078(n+3)`) |
| height at most 5 | `n = 1…` | `1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 31, 61, 120` | pentanacci `1.9659` | [A001591](https://oeis.org/A001591) (`= A001591(n+4)`) |

*(Every row agrees with enumeration of compositions for `n ≤ 14` and with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16.)*

### Tower-spacing skylines

Skylines on `{1, …, h}` in which every row `2, …, h` has its empty runs between filled cells at least `g` long, so towers that reach a row are at least `g` columns apart ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]). A column-by-column transfer matrix counts them.

The `h = 3` row is Hardin's table [A217883](https://oeis.org/A217883), the `h = 4` row [A217954](https://oeis.org/A217954), and the `g = 3` column [A228461](https://oeis.org/A228461). Every cell agrees with the OEIS data at the stated offset for `w ≤ 24`, and its minimal recurrence order, found by Berlekamp-Massey on 90 terms, is `(h − 1)g + 1`, 2026-10-16.)*

The `h = 2` row, `A005251`, `A005252`, `A005253`, `A005689` and `A098574`, has the closed form `Sum_k C(w+g−(g−1)k, 2k)` ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]).

### The Pell castle strip: 1-smooth strips on {1, 2, 3}

Skylines on `{1, 2, 3}` whose neighboring heights differ by at most 1 ([[pell-castle-strip](pages/pell-castle-strip.md)]); the condition on the end columns picks the sequence.

| object | from | first terms | growth | OEIS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| first column at height 1 | `w = 1…` | `1, 2, 5, 12, 29, 70, 169, 408` | `1+√2` | [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129) (`= A000129(w)`) Pell numbers (`= P⋆_w`; width g.f. `x/(1−2x−x²)`) |
| any first column | `w = 1…` | `3, 7, 17, 41, 99, 239, 577, 1393` | `1+√2` | [A001333](https://oeis.org/A001333) (`= A001333(w+1)`) Pell-Lucas numbers |

### 1-smooth castles of height h

The 1-smooth rule on `{1, …, h}` ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]) extends the Pell rows to `h = 2, …, 12`. `strips(w, h)` counts the skylines on `{1, …, h}` with first column at height 1, and `smooth(w, h)` those of height `h`, with g.f. `x^h/(η_h η_{h−1})`.

### m-smooth castles of height h

Skylines whose neighboring columns differ by at most `m`, with first column at height 1 ([[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)]), for `m = 2, 3, 4`. For `h ≤ m + 1` every skyline qualifies, so with the first column at height 1 the castles of width `w ≥ 2` and height `h` number `h^{w−1} − (h−1)^{w−1}`; with any first column they number `A(w, h) = h^w − (h−1)^w`, with even-block part `A^e(w, h)`.

### Motzkin castles

A **Motzkin-path castle** is a 1-smooth skyline (`|c_{i+1} − c_i| ≤ 1`) with both end columns at height 1 ([[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]). Its heights minus 1 form a Motzkin path of length `w − 1`, and its block count is `1 + #up-steps`, so the even-block castles are the Motzkin paths with an odd number of up-steps.

### Zig-zag strips and zig-zag castles

Skylines whose neighboring columns differ by exactly 1, the 1-smooth and plateau-free rules imposed together, with transfer matrix `A_path` ([[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]). `zstrips(w, h) = 𝟙ᵀ A_path^{w−1} 𝟙` counts the zig-zag strips on `{1, …, h}`, which the OEIS counts as zig-zag paths in a rectangle of width `h`, and `A_zigzag(w, h) = zstrips(w, h) − zstrips(w, h − 1)` the zig-zag castles of height `h`, in bijection with the `(h − 1)`-balanced strings of length `w − 1`. The color of a zig-zag path is the parity of its first column `c_1`.

### Mersenne strips and Mersenne castles

Castles whose neighboring columns, read as strings whose lengths are the column heights, sound a perfect consonance: heights in ratio 1, 2, 3/2 or 4/3, or the inverse ([[mersenne-castles](pages/mersenne-castles.md)]). `mstrips(w, h) = 𝟙ᵀ M_cons^{w−1} 𝟙` counts the Mersenne strips on `{1, …, h}` and `A_Mersenne(w, h) = mstrips(w, h) − mstrips(w, h − 1)` the Mersenne castles of height `h`. A consonance keeps the part of a height prime to 6, so `A_Mersenne(w, h) = A_Mersenne(w, h₀)` for `h₀` the largest divisor of `h` of the form `2^a 3^b`, and the rows are at those heights.

### Ridge strips and ridge castles

The ridge rule: neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height `h`, with transfer matrix `R_h = J − D` ([[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)], [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]). The ridge strips are the skylines on `{1, …, h}` under the rule, and the ridge castles those of height `h`, `𝟙ᵀR_h^{w−1}𝟙 − (h−1)(h−2)^{w−1}` of them; their even-block part is on [[proper-castle-projection](pages/proper-castle-projection.md)].

### Signed tower count P(k, ·) rows

The signed tower count `P(k, L) = Σ (−1)^{blocks}` in the base length `L` at fixed tower height `k` ([[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)]), with a linear recurrence of order `k + 1`. The even-`k` rows are positive (checked `k ≤ 12`, `L < 40`); for odd `k` the roots of largest modulus are a complex-conjugate pair and the rows change sign in runs.

### Strip Perron-root sequences

Width counts of the 0/1 transfer-matrix strips of [[reachable-field-census](pages/reachable-field-census.md)] and [[metallic-strip-realizability](pages/metallic-strip-realizability.md)].

| object | from | first terms | growth | OEIS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the plastic strip (height 3, rule `1 → 3`, `2 → 1`, `3 → {1, 2}`) | `w = 1…` | `3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 16, 21, 28, …` | `ψ` | [A000931](https://oeis.org/A000931) (`= A000931(w+9)`) Padovan (checked `w ≤ 40`); these are the maximal Fibonacci castles of width `w + 3` |

The quadratic strips off the line `p₂ = 1` reach the fields `Q(√17)`, `Q(√21)`, `Q(√6)`, `Q(√7)` and `Q(√33)`, each through several strip matrices, so a field has no single count sequence.

### Castles by semi-perimeter

### Prime castles by area

Gluing castles at a shared column of height 1 makes a free monoid; its primes correspond to the castles with no column of height 1, the prime castles, `F_{n−1}` of them of area `n` ([[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]). A convex castle has at most one prime factor ([[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)]). Terms from `n = 2` unless stated.

| object | first terms | g.f. / formula | OEIS |

| prime castles | `1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21` | `q²/(1−q−q²)` | [A000045](https://oeis.org/A000045) (`= A000045(n−1) = F_{n−1}`; compositions into parts `≥ 2`) |

### Tree castles by area at fixed height

Tree castles, the castles with no `2 × 2` square, of height 2 and of height at most `h ≥ 3`, by area `n` ([[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)]). For `h ≥ 3` the count at area `n` is the number of compositions of `n + 1` into parts `{1, 3, 4, …, h + 1}`; at height 2 it is the number of compositions of `n + 1` into parts `{1, 3}` that use a 3. Terms from `n = 1`. Without a bound on the height the count is `A005251(n+2)` (section *Multi-interpretation hub*).

| object | first terms | g.f. / formula | OEIS |

| height 2 | `0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 18, 27, 40` | parts `{1, 3}`, using a 3; `A000930(n+1) − 1` | [A077868](https://oeis.org/A077868) (`= A077868(n−2)`; `n ≥ 2`) |
| height at most 3 | `1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 15, 25, 40, 64, 104` | parts `{1, 3, 4}` | [A006498](https://oeis.org/A006498) (`= A006498(n+1)`) g.f. denominator `(1 + q²)(1 − q − q²)`, golden by area |
| height at most 4 | `1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 18, 31, 53, 89, 149` | parts `{1, 3, 4, 5}` | [A000570](https://oeis.org/A000570) (`= A000570(n+1)`), tournaments determined by their score vectors |

- [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)] - the Motzkin rows: cornerless Motzkin paths, the parity split of `M_{w−1}`, the Motzkin paths of bounded height, and the rows by semi-perimeter.
- [[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)] - the zig-zag strips and castles, the zig-zag paths of the OEIS and the balanced strings.
- [[oeis-mining-pe502](pages/oeis-mining-pe502.md)] - the castle counts matched to OEIS entries, among them the difference-of-powers, height-2, signed tower, convex and area rows.
